record.paper_title: Jet tomography in heavy-ion collisions - Challenges, Results, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Status of conformal AdS/CFT energy loss
record.original_question: Is a conformal AdS/CFT jet-energy-loss scenario, characterized by a fixed jet-medium coupling and expected flat nuclear modification factor RAA, viable after the first LHC nuclear-modification-factor data showed a distinct RAA(pT) slope and a rapid rise of measured RAA(pT), or is the conformal scenario ruled out by those data?

evidence.quote: Besides this, conformal AdS/CFT energy loss was expected to yield a flat RAA [38]. However, the distinct slope of the pQCD prediction for the nuclear modification factor at LHC energies given in Ref. [24] was shown to be correct, resulting in the question if (conformal) AdS/CFT was ruled out by the first data of the LHC and how to resolve the puzzle connected to the pre-LHC runs.

In case of a conformal AdS-scenario with a squared path-length dependence, however, the nuclear modification factor is clearly overquenched [40]. The reason is that a conformal AdS-scenario is characterized by a fixed jet-medium coupling since a conformal theory does not have any additional scale which can run. Thus, we concluded [40] that a conformal scenario is ruled out by the rapid rise of the measured RAA(pT).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider high transverse-momentum partons (jets) traversing the hot, deconfined QCD medium produced in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The nuclear modification factor R_AA(p_T) is defined as the ratio of the measured charged-hadron transverse-momentum spectrum in nucleus-nucleus collisions to the spectrum in proton-proton collisions at the same center-of-mass energy, scaled by the average number of binary nucleon-nucleon collisions.

A "conformal AdS/CFT energy-loss scenario" is one in which the medium is modeled by a strongly coupled conformal field theory (e.g. N=4 super Yang-Mills) with a fixed (non-running) jet-medium coupling, leading via the gauge/gravity correspondence to an energy-loss law of the form dE/dx ∝ x^2 (path-length squared) for a light quark or gluon traversing the medium. Because the underlying theory is conformal, no additional scale enters and the coupling does not run with p_T.

Question: Under such a conformal AdS/CFT energy-loss scenario, the predicted R_AA(p_T) at LHC energies (Pb–Pb collisions at center-of-mass energies of several TeV per nucleon pair) is approximately flat as a function of p_T at high p_T. The measured R_AA(p_T) at LHC, however, exhibits a pronounced rising slope with p_T. Determine whether the conformal AdS/CFT energy-loss scenario, with its fixed jet-medium coupling and squared-path-length dependence, is compatible with the observed rapid rise of R_AA(p_T) in LHC data, or whether it is excluded by these measurements.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is treated as resolved in the heavy-ion phenomenology literature: comparisons of conformal AdS/CFT energy-loss predictions (fixed coupling, dE/dx ∝ x^2) with LHC R_AA(p_T) measurements show overquenching and a flat shape inconsistent with the observed rising slope, leading the community to conclude that a strictly conformal AdS scenario is ruled out, while non-conformal/running-coupling holographic extensions remain under study.
